evidence.title: 内务府现行则例 on 惠济祠, 河神庙 (as quoted in S47)
evidence.excerpt_zh: 八月奉旨：谕御园内仿照江南规制建立惠济祠、河神庙二所，岁时陛香展礼，因思清漪园、静明园两处龙神庙均有春秋致祭典礼，御园惠济祠、河神庙显应尤昭允宜，特奉明禋以光祀典，著于每岁春秋二季一体致祭，届期奏派管理圆明园大臣一员肃恭将事，即自本年秋季为始。
evidence.summary: Both shrines copy those of Jiangnan, in the Huai'an area, and get state sacrifice each spring and autumn from 1817.

evidence.title: 嘉庆 《惠济祠河神庙拈香敬述》 and 自注 (as quoted in S47)
evidence.excerpt_zh: 建祠祈妥佑，数载沐神恩。恬浪固河堰，安澜达海门。承天施渥泽，率土靖黎元。永戴平成德，感衷诚述言。 / 御园之南惠济祠、河神庙建于癸酉秋间，所以妥佾明神，时致亲祈，俾东南亿万民生同等衽席者也。
evidence.summary: Jiaqing prays at the two water-god shrines on the south of the garden, built from autumn 1813, for the safety of river dykes and grain transport.

evidence.title: 惠济祠河神庙瞻礼述事
evidence.locator: v4 p.333, under 惠济祠; source ref 5-327
evidence.excerpt_zh: 东南财赋区，亿万民生置。转漕靖河淮，国家之巨事。遥仰惠济祠，大典举非易。御园致敬诚，绘像命疆吏。赫奕悬宝龛，如莅清江地。从兹永安澜，神恩普荫庇。清江浦，为河淮交汇之处。濒河郡邑，亿万民生，视水势为安危。而七省全漕，皆由此转运。是以国家置设重臣及文武员弁，专司修防疏浚之事，督臣时复履视而董率之。康熙、乾隆年间，屡经亲临相度，指示机宜。河壖崇建河神庙，向称惠济祠，屡显灵佑。予于甲辰年恭随皇考南巡，曾侍升香瞻礼。当年巡方举典，所重在民生俾乂也。惟是典巨费繁，举行
evidence.summary: Poem 惠济祠河神庙瞻礼述事 by the Jiaqing Emperor, 1814, filed by the editors under 惠济祠.

evidence.title: 惠济祠河神庙瞻礼敬述
evidence.locator: v4 p.334, under 惠济祠; source ref 6-107
evidence.excerpt_zh: 神像绘南省，迎来禁苑中。三江众水汇，千里一诚通。永沐安澜庆，常叨惠泽隆。国家最要政，叩祝竭微衷。
evidence.summary: Poem 惠济祠河神庙瞻礼敬述 by the Jiaqing Emperor, 1815, filed by the editors under 惠济祠.

evidence.title: 惠济祠河神庙瞻礼敬纪
evidence.locator: v4 p.334, under 惠济祠; source ref 6-215
evidence.excerpt_zh: 建祠申素志，从此沐安澜。河底日深畅，海门岁展宽。惟神宏佑厚，览我寸诚殚。千里一心应，敬勤朂庶官。
evidence.summary: Poem 惠济祠河神庙瞻礼敬纪 by the Jiaqing Emperor, 1816, filed by the editors under 惠济祠.

evidence.title: 惠济祠河神庙谢恩瞻礼敬述
evidence.locator: v4 p.335, under 惠济祠; source ref 6-259
evidence.excerpt_zh: 建祠御苑感居歆，连岁安澜慰寸心。河道畅通永恬静，海门刷涤日宽深。黄淮相济平成庆，扬豫全消昬垫侵。诚谢神恩惠亿兆，瓣香升鼎致予忱。
evidence.summary: Poem 惠济祠河神庙谢恩瞻礼敬述 by the Jiaqing Emperor, 1816, filed by the editors under 惠济祠.

evidence.title: 惠济祠河神庙瞻礼敬述
evidence.locator: v4 p.335, under 惠济祠; source ref 6-368
evidence.excerpt_zh: 诚敬感通速，建祠沐泽鸿。堤工益巩固，海口倍深通。顺轨全河畅，安澜三省同。升香致虔谢，福佑锡绥丰。
evidence.summary: Poem 惠济祠河神庙瞻礼敬述 by the Jiaqing Emperor, 1817, filed by the editors under 惠济祠.

evidence.title: 绮春园 after 1860, yaffin 系列15
evidence.summary: Lead: says the gate district, 庄严法界, 惠济祠, 湛清轩 and 绿满轩 survived in 1860, the garden was renamed 万春园 under Tongzhi, and was destroyed in 1900, with only 正觉寺 standing. The south gate dates from 1809 and 新宫门 is its later name. Unverified compilation.

evidence.title: 祭器 由运料门 (S47 section 4)
evidence.summary: A file of 1817 says ritual vessels for the spring and autumn rites at 惠济祠 and 河神庙 were carried in by garden labourers from outside 运料门 and carried back out by it: a working gate of the garden on the Qichun side.

evidence.title: 贾珺: 惠济祠, 河神庙 from Yangshi Lei drawings and 圆明园匾额略节
evidence.summary: Side by side, 惠济祠 east: three-bay main hall with three-bay east and west side halls north of it. 河神庙 west: one court, three-bay main hall, three-bay flanking halls. Plaques are listed; 惠济祠 holds a tablet of the sea goddess 天后, 河神庙 tablets of the Huai river god, 金龙四大王 and 黄大王.

evidence.title: 1861 年 五处上供 (S47 section 4)
evidence.summary: In the fifth month of 1861 offerings were still made at five surviving places: the 春雨轩 earth-god shrine, 吕祖亭 at 双鹤斋, the 观音庵 at 课农轩, and 河神庙 and 惠济祠 of Qichun Yuan. It says only that these were standing and in use after the fire.

evidence.title: 绮春园 at the end of 1860
evidence.summary: Per S220 the garden was burned on the 5th day of the 9th lunar month of 1860 (18 October) by British troops, except 正觉寺, 惠济祠 and 河神庙. 常嫔, who stayed behind ill, died of the shock.

evidence.title: 贾珺, 圆明三园中的祀庙祠宇建筑探析, 故宫博物院院刊 2012(3)
evidence.summary: A survey of the 33 shrines of the three gardens, with dates and forms: ancestor halls, flower god and dragon king temples, 河神庙, 关帝庙. The first thing to read for small temples with little else. Assigned here by type, not checked per temple.

evidence.title: 圆明园百景史事分景汇编: 惠济祠、河神庙
evidence.locator: from p.307, under 惠济祠、河神庙
evidence.summary: Spring and autumn state sacrifices at these two shrines were ordered in 1817, led by the minister in charge of the garden. The listed sacrifices run on after 1860, to 1883; S361 says the shrines survived 1860. 惠济祠、河神庙: 47 dated items, 1817-1883, of which 0 poems and 47 court records (Jiaqing, Daoguang, Xianfeng, Tongzhi, Guangxu); recurring themes: state papers, visits to the dowager. First dated 1817, last dated 1883.

evidence.title: 圆明园五朝御制诗文集注 v4, editors' note on 绮春园
evidence.summary: Formed from princes' and ministers' gardens, about 54.3 ha. Taken back from Fuheng's heirs and renamed in 1769; gate, tiger-stone wall and 正觉寺 added by 1773, rebuilt in 1795. Jiaqing's growth came in three stages: the western and central groups of the Thirty Scenes first, then the new gate and eastern scenes, finally the south-west (招凉榭, 湛清轩, 畅和堂, 澄心堂, the shrines), gathered as a New Twenty Scenes.

evidence.title: 圆明园五朝御制诗文集注 v4, editors' note on 惠济祠
evidence.summary: Begun 1813 as the garden's own shrines, with rites each spring and autumn. 惠济祠 holds the tablet of the Heavenly Consort; 河神庙 to the west has three niches for river deities. The editors say both survived 1860, with garden staff still on guard and offerings kept up, and were lost around 1900: this answers why the rites of S360 run on.

searched: No picture of it found in the Forty Scenes album, its 1745 woodcuts, the Bertin gouaches and the 1887 lithograph; the 20 Xiyang Lou plates; ruin photographs on Commons, at Östasiatiska museet, the Slovene Ethnographic Museum and Historical Photographs of China; today's photographs on Commons.
